      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'

        - address

## What I did

The `POST /api/owners` endpoint previously bound the body and built the owner in one `BuildOwner` step with only the generated `@Valid` constraints. Those constraints don't reject a whitespace-only `address`/`city` (they only have `minLength: 1`, which `"   "` satisfies), and when they do fire they produce a `schemaValidationErrors` ProblemDetail — not the `errors` array the spec requires. So I added an explicit validation step following the project's OfficeFloor conventions:

1. **`ValidateOwnerFields`** (new function class) — now the first step of the POST pipeline. It binds `@RequestBody` once, checks each of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` for null-or-blank (`String.isBlank()`, so whitespace counts as missing), throws a checked `MissingOwnerFieldsException` listing the offending field names, and otherwise republishes the body as a variable.

2. **`MissingOwnerFieldsException`** (new checked exception) — carries the list of missing field names.

3. **`MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler`** + its escalation YAML — responds `400` with body `{"errors": [...]}`.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — added the `validate` step first (`next: build`).

5. **`BuildOwner`** — now reads the validated body via `@Val OwnerFieldsDto` instead of re-binding `@RequestBody` (only one step per pipeline may bind the body).

The three acceptance tests — missing `city` → 400 with `errors` containing `"city"`, blank telephone → 400, and complete owner → 2xx — all pass.
